newsitem.title: USA: Job cuts soar to 15-month high, survey says.
newsitem.headline: Job cuts soar to 15-month high, survey says.

text.p: The economic numbers may be painting a rosy picture of the jobs market, but the good times did not keep companies from cutting jobs last month at the fastest pace in 15 months, a survey by a leading outplacement firm said Tuesday.
Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc., which tracks job cuts nationwide, said 50,182 workers lost their jobs in March, up 33.9 percent from 37,486 in March of last year.
Last month's layoffs were the largest monthly cut since January, 1996, when 97,379 jobs were lost, it said.

"We are no longer seeing the blockbuster cuts in the tens of thousands that cause big headlines," said John Challenger, executive vice president of Challenger, Gray & Christmas. "Instead, we are seeing cuts of 2,500, 3,000 and 5,000," he said.

The industry sectors with the most job cuts were the aerospace-defence (5,694), computers (4,897), financial services (4,645), retail (4,366), transportation (4,188), automotive (4,098), services (3,600), industrial goods (3,540), consumer goods, (3,523), and food (3,340).

"Last month's figure may be evidence that the Federal Reserve Board may have jumped the gun in raising interest rates, perhaps not taking into full account the measures companies are taking to self-correct," Challenger said.
Last month the Fed raised short-term interest rates by a quarter percentage point, the first increase in more than two years, in an effort to head off inflation and slow the economy's growth.
The rate hike set off a chain reaction that boosted borrowing costs for consumers and corporations, fuelling concern that the tighter monetary policy could hurt the economy.

Many companies fear inflation as much as Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, "because they know that if they try to pass on higher costs to customers they will be eaten alive by competition," Challenger said.
The econony continues in a fast track, with the Labour Department reporting last week that the jobless rate fell to 5.2 percent last month from 5.3 percent and hourly wages rose.
It said 175,000 non-farm jobs were added to payrolls in March, vs. a gain of 293,000 in February.

Challenger said 134,257 jobs were slashed during the first quarter of 1997, 17 percent more than in the fourth quarter of 1996. But the 1997 quarter was down 20.4 percent compared with the first quarter of 1996, which included large layoffs at AT&T Corp., it said.
